one_liner: Pure-Rust glyph loading, scaling, positioning and rasterization crate; rewrite of rusttype with cheaper per-glyph layout, especially for CFF fonts.
what_it_does: ab_glyph parses TrueType and OpenType fonts (.ttf, CFF-flavoured .otf, variable fonts, collections by index) through ttf-parser and exposes a `Font` trait (glyph_id, advances, side bearings, legacy kern-table kerning, ascent/descent) plus `ScaleFont` for pixel-scaled metrics. A `Glyph` is a plain (id, scale, position) value; `outline_glyph` turns it into an `OutlinedGlyph` whose `draw(|x, y, coverage|)` callback rasterizes it with the companion zero-dependency ab_glyph_rasterizer crate. The crate does not lay out text itself (the paragraph layout in the benchmarks is example code in the unpublished dev crate; glyph_brush_layout builds on ab_glyph for that). It is not a drop-in for rusttype: there is no `Font::layout`, no `PositionedGlyph` with eagerly computed pixel bounds, and no equivalent of rusttype's gpu_cache feature in this repository.
how_it_is_fast: Mostly API design: layout yields lightweight `Glyph` values and defers outlining and bounding boxes until `outline_glyph`/`glyph_bounds`, whereas rusttype 0.9's `positioned()` computed a pixel bounding box for every glyph during layout via ttf-parser `glyph_bounding_box`, which for CFF fonts runs the full charstring outliner (ttf-parser 0.5/0.6 read the stored glyf bbox for .ttf but outlined CFF glyphs) - this is where the large .otf gap comes from. Since 0.2.12 it also pre-parses the Unicode cmap and horizontal kern subtables once at font load (owned_ttf_parser `PreParsedSubtables`), which the changelog credits with 25-30% faster layout benchmarks. The rasterizer is a font-rs-derived signed-area accumulation rasterizer: line segments add signed coverage deltas into a float buffer and one running-sum pass (`for_each_pixel`) produces coverage; quadratics are flattened by a deviation-based segment count and cubics by stb_truetype-style recursive midpoint subdivision. Line drawing is the same scalar code compiled with `#[target_feature(enable = "avx2")]` and `sse4.2` and chosen once at runtime (compiler auto-vectorization, no hand-written intrinsics).
when_to_use: Rust code that needs char-to-glyph mapping, advances, simple kerning and coverage rasterization of individual glyphs (game UIs, GPU text atlases via glyph_brush, plotting and image libraries such as plotters and imageproc already depend on it).

Migrating from rusttype 0.9, especially with CFF .otf fonts: layout cost no longer depends on outline complexity (the 2020 table shows ab_glyph at 11.1 us for both the Exo2 .ttf and .otf, rusttype at 17.3 us and 98.1 us).
no_std or wasm targets: CI builds both crates for thumbv6m-none-eabi (no default features, libm) and wasm32-unknown-unknown; FontArc works on no_std targets with pointer atomics since 0.2.32.
Left-to-right scripts without contextual shaping, where per-pair kerning from a legacy 'kern' table (or none) is acceptable.
When you want a widely deployed, small-dependency crate: about 45.2 million crates.io downloads and 269 reverse dependencies.
when_not_to_use: Complex scripts, ligatures, mark positioning or any OpenType feature: there is no GSUB/GPOS support (issue #74 'OTF feature tags' open since 2023-02); use HarfBuzz/HarfRust or a layout stack such as Parley or cosmic-text.
Fonts that kern only through GPOS (common in modern OpenType fonts): `kern` reads only the legacy 'kern' table subtables, so those pairs come back unkerned.

Raw rasterization throughput is the bottleneck: sibling entries report faster pure-Rust rasterizers (fontdue's own plots versus ab_glyph 0.2.3; TiTanF's README medians put Fontdue ahead of ab_glyph at 10-160 px). There is no hinting, so small-size output will not match FreeType hinted rendering.

Supply-chain policies that block unmaintained dependencies: ttf-parser, its parsing backend, is flagged RUSTSEC-2026-0192 (informational, unmaintained, 2026-06-28); the Skrifa port (PR #122) is a draft, needs a breaking release, and its author measured it slower (about 70 us TrueType and 90 us CFF vs about 55 us with ttf-parser on the layout-and-outline benchmark).
C or C++ projects: it is a Rust crate with no C API; calling it from C++ requires your own FFI layer.

integration.form: crate (ab_glyph plus the separately published ab_glyph_rasterizer)
integration.dependencies: owned_ttf_parser 0.25 (wraps ttf-parser), ab_glyph_rasterizer 0.1 (no dependencies); optional libm for no_std
integration.min_toolchain: Latest stable Rust only (README policy; no rust-version field in Cargo.toml); edition 2021
integration.platforms: any Rust target; CI tests on ubuntu-latest (x86-64) and builds thumbv6m-none-eabi (no_std + libm) and wasm32-unknown-unknown; runtime AVX2/SSE4.2 dispatch for line drawing on x86/x86_64 with the std feature
integration.thread_safety: FontArc wraps `Arc<dyn Font + Send + Sync>` for sharing a font across threads; each `OutlinedGlyph::draw` call builds its own Rasterizer, so drawing holds no shared mutable state. No further thread-safety documentation.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial - same author and concepts as rusttype, but a different API: no Font::layout iterator, no PositionedGlyph with pixel bounds, no gpu_cache; ports need code changes

gotchas: Coverage values are not clamped: since ab_glyph_rasterizer 0.1.5 a value of 1.0 or more means fully covered. Open issue #121 (2025-08-20) reports tiny non-zero coverage (about 1.6e-7) outside glyphs from floating-point cancellation in draw_line_scalar, visible as shadows when glyphs are drawn repeatedly; the reporter's workaround rounds coverage.
Out-of-bounds panics in draw_line_scalar were fixed in three rounds (rasterizer 0.1.3, 0.1.9 in 2025-06, 0.1.10 in 2025-08); make sure the lockfile has ab_glyph_rasterizer 0.1.10 or later.
`OutlinedGlyph::draw` allocates a fresh width x height float buffer for every call; cache rasterized glyphs (as glyph_brush does) rather than redrawing per frame.
Missing characters map silently to GlyphId(0) (.notdef) rather than returning None; some `Font` default methods return None or 0.0 where fonts lack data (issue #99 open).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ab_glyph over fontdue or TiTanF when you need CFF .otf and variable-font support, no_std, and compatibility with the glyph_brush/imageproc/plotters ecosystem, accepting a slower rasterizer by those projects' own measurements; it is a higher-level glyph API than Fontations' skrifa or ttf-parser (which it builds on), and it does no shaping, so Parley or a HarfBuzz port is the choice once text needs real OpenType layout.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Criterion runs from May 2020 (ab_glyph 0.1 against rusttype 0.9; rustc version, flags and CPU not stated) laid out one 225-character sentence with Exo2 Light at 25 px: 11.1 us vs 17.3 us for .ttf (1.56x) and 11.1 us vs 98.1 us for .otf (8.85x); the first README version (2020-05-08) also showed an OpenSans-Italic .ttf row at 19.3 vs 25.3 us (1.31x) that was removed three days later in 'Simplify bench comparison'. The two harnesses do different work: rusttype's layout computes a pixel bounding box per glyph (a stored glyf bbox read for .ttf, a full CFF outline pass for .otf in ttf-parser 0.5/0.6) while ab_glyph defers it and additionally wraps lines at 600 px, so the ratio measures work avoided by ab_glyph's API rather than the same computation done faster.
status_note: Apache-2.0 and copyable; last release ab_glyph 0.2.32 on 2025-09-28 with only lint, CI and test-hash commits since (latest 2026-08-30), so effectively in maintenance mode while the unmaintained ttf-parser backend awaits the draft Skrifa port.
